title: Project Setup and Cargo.toml Configuration
description: Create the Rust project structure with Cargo.toml specifying dependencies for complex number support, testing, and documentation. Set up the module layout for the FFT library including src/, tests/, and Cargo.toml.
notes: This is the foundational task. All subsequent tasks depend on this being complete.

title: Complex Number Implementation
description: Implement a basic complex number type in Rust that supports construction, arithmetic operations (+, -, *, /), magnitude calculation, and conjugation. This will serve as the foundation for all FFT operations.
notes: Use std::arch::complex as a reference but implement a domain-specific variant that matches C's complex.h conventions.

title: Core FFT Algorithm Implementation
description: Implement the Cooley-Tukey radix-2 FFT algorithm in Rust. This is the most critical task — it must faithfully translate the C source FFT implementation while using Rust idioms. Focus on: input/output array handling, bit-reversal permutation, recursive/iterative butterfly operations, and normalization.
notes: If the C source uses iterative FFT, implement the same approach. Pay special attention to the exact butterfly computation formula. Consider whether to use unsafe blocks for pointer manipulation or pure Rust approaches.

title: Memory Management Translation
description: Translate C memory allocation/deallocation patterns (malloc, calloc, realloc, free) to their Rust equivalents (Box, Vec, alloc, drop). Implement safe wrappers for common C memory patterns used in FFT implementations (pre-allocated buffers, temporary arrays, result storage).
notes: Create a memory_management module that provides idiomatic Rust wrappers around C-style memory operations. Include tests verifying correct memory lifecycle.

title: FFT Utility Functions and Helpers
description: Implement utility functions commonly found in FFT libraries: next_power_of_two, fft_size_parity_check, bit-reversal permutation, pre/post processing for real-input FFTs. These are typically small but essential building blocks.
notes: These utilities are often the bulk of a C FFT library's non-algorithm code. Ensure they handle edge cases correctly.

title: Integration Tests and Verification
description: Write comprehensive integration tests that verify the translated FFT library produces results identical to the original C implementation. Compare against known test vectors (e.g., small input sets, known FFT outputs). Include both forward and inverse FFT tests.
notes: This is the final verification step. The test harness should accept the original C FFT output as a reference and compare against Rust output within numerical tolerance.
